This binary outcome is modeled through a step function or sigmoidal approximation in GSI's Bayesian framework. The unreinforced evocation count (n) acts as a degradation parameter that asymptotically approaches zero as extinction occurs. In GSE, this manifests as a Markovian state transition where each evocation updates the internal model of stimulus-response associations. The key duality lies between initial high sensitivity (pre-conditioning) and subsequent suppression (post-conditioning), reflected in the vertical displacement of the origin relative to T_r. This shift is not merely empirical but represents a fundamental reconfiguration of the agent’s perceptual-motor interface. Failure modes include premature extinction due to excessive reinforcement or persistent overreaction due to insufficient conditioning. These behaviors are captured through variance in n and ΔT respectively.
